topic: humanoid foundation models: world models, VLAs, robot brains, embodied AI research, model releases, training data, simulation, compute

items.title: DEF CON's robot hacks become a free Isaac Sim test suite
items.summary: Trend Micro subsidiary VicOne has released a free Radeis extension for NVIDIA Isaac Sim that lets developers replay adversarial visual prompts, malicious inputs and sensor manipulation attacks against their own robot models in simulation. The scenarios build on a DEF CON 34 robot-hacking challenge where 16 teams logged 25 successful solves, according to the company.

items.title: Highlanders' KEPLER folds planning and reflexes into one world model
items.summary: The Tokyo firm's foundation world model unifies long-horizon reasoning with low-latency control, letting a robot evaluate outcomes through predictive world modeling before acting and keep improving from fleet data, according to Highlanders. Rated 9/10 on humanoid.guide's Brain Score scale, KEPLER comes from the same firm whose roughly 1.75 m humanoid Mitsubishi Motors plans to mass-produce in Kyoto from 2027.

items.title: Figure 03 climbs a ladder — Adcock calls it fully autonomous
items.summary: A new video shows the Figure 03 humanoid ascending a ladder with no visible human intervention — 'fully autonomous,' according to founder Brett Adcock, whose Helix system pairs visual perception with whole-body motion control. Figure has not disclosed the control stack behind the clip, and repeatability, speed and whether the setup was staged all remain unverified.

items.title: Unitree folds hearing, sight and control into one G1 brain
items.summary: UnifoLM OminiA runs Unitree's G1 as a single system — handling spoken requests, visual scenes, task reasoning and interruption recovery in one framework, with household jobs like laundry sorting and dishwasher loading as the pitch, according to the company. Code and weights stay closed for this version, which is offered via backorder rather than as finished mass-market software.

items.title: Reimagine Robotics wants workers, not programmers, to teach robots
items.summary: Founded by leaders of Google DeepMind's applied robotics group, the London- and Sydney-based startup has emerged from stealth with pre-seed backing from Fly Ventures and firstminute capital, building systems that let front-line workers teach robots by demonstration and correct them mid-task. Its first cells are tending 3D printers and disassembling hard drives for materials recovery, and prototyping a new behavior has shrunk from about a day to roughly 10 minutes, according to the company.

items.title: Five platforms are becoming physical AI's infrastructure layer
items.summary: NVIDIA's simulation-and-compute stack, Applied Intuition's validation tooling, Scale AI's data factory, Hugging Face's open-source LeRobot layer and Lightwheel's Real2Sim2Real loop are hardening into the load-bearing infrastructure of robot intelligence, according to The Robot Report's analysis. Scale says it now collects more than 1,000 hours of demonstration data a day, after delivering over 150,000 hours of physical AI data to robotics customers in 2025.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2 controls humanoids from feet to fingertips
items.summary: Google DeepMind's new model family pairs a vision-language-action model that runs a full humanoid — walking, crouching and working 22-DOF five-fingered hands — with an embodied-reasoning model that plans multi-step tasks and coordinates teams of different robots, according to Google DeepMind. An on-device variant adapts to a new robot body in a few hours from under 200 examples, with Apptronik, Boston Dynamics and Agile Robots among the launch partners.

items.title: Enigma raises $71M to make robot brains people can use
items.summary: The Israeli-Californian lab emerged from stealth with a $71 million seed led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, building AI models and interfaces meant to make any robot as intuitive to command as a car's volume knob, according to the company. Alongside the round, Enigma put what it calls the world's first interactive AI robotics experience online — 100 real robots the public can drive at robots.online.

items.title: IEEE Humanoids 2026 puts robot labor at the top of the agenda
items.summary: The 25th IEEE-RAS Humanoids conference lands in Santa Clara this December under the theme 'Humanoids and the Future of Work', putting deployment governance and worker impact alongside actuators and reinforcement learning. A loco-manipulation challenge will benchmark 10–15 academic and commercial teams on standardized factory-style tasks.

items.title: Robot training data becomes a manufacturing business
items.summary: Encord has turned a San Leandro facility into a data factory where camera- and sensor-rigged human 'pilots' produce the demonstrations robot models are starving for — an adequate dataset would need something like five times YouTube's video corpus, according to the company. Germany's Zander Labs is testing a stranger input: headsets that read error, intent and surprise from trainers' brains to flag when a model needs the most compute, according to TechCrunch.

items.title: Generalist says GEN-1 now transfers across hands, tools and grippers
items.summary: Generalist has shown its GEN-1 foundation model driving five-fingered hands, power tools and custom grippers from a single base model — even adapting mid-task when the end effector is swapped, according to the company. GEN-1 was pretrained on more than half a million hours of real interaction data covering roughly 9,000 end-effector variations, Generalist says.

items.title: NEURA and RWTH Aachen are building a 3,000 m² gym for robot experience
items.summary: NEURA Robotics and RWTH Aachen University will open a 3,000-square-meter Physical AI training center on the Melaten campus by the end of 2026, where robots collect the real-world interaction data that simulation alone can't deliver. It is one of ten NEURA Gyms planned worldwide — five running across Europe, the US and China by year-end, according to the company, whose CEO David Reger says the biggest bottleneck in Physical AI 'is no longer intelligence, it's experience.'

items.title: Friction is the input robot world models are missing
items.summary: Vision and joint encoders can't capture contact physics, argues Contactile CEO Heba Khamis — she proposes a 'vision-μ-action' class of models conditioned on real-time friction measurement, shifting world models from statistical pattern-matching toward causal understanding of why grasps succeed or fail.

items.title: Generalist AI puts GEN-1 to work on Elite's cobots
items.summary: The Nvidia-backed startup founded by ex-DeepMind researchers will use Elite Robots' industrial cobots for real-world data collection and validation of its GEN-1 foundation model — a pairing that has already logged 1,800+ block stackings with zero interventions at a 99% task success rate, according to Elite Robots.

items.title: Tencent stacks three robot brains into its Tairos platform
items.summary: At WAIC in Shanghai, Tencent rolled out a full-stack embodied intelligence offering — pairing the Hy-Embodied-VLA-0.5 action model with the VLM-1.0 perception and RxBrain-1.0 reasoning models under a new TairosAgent framework, according to Tencent. The Tairos platform, first launched in 2025, now ships open-source tools and cloud services for robot developers.

items.title: Flexion's CEO warns robotics is stuck in the teleoperation trap
items.summary: Teleop datasets are over 100,000 times smaller than what trains today's language models, Nikita Rudin argues — and reinforcement learning, not an endless stream of human demonstrations, is the way out.

items.title: Sunday calls laundry 'solved' as ACT-2 folds at 99%
items.summary: The Memo maker's new foundation model folded clothes in homes it had never seen at a 99.1% success rate — 778 of 785 attempts, zero-shot with no per-home fine-tuning, according to Sunday Robotics, though the figures are the company's own evaluation. ACT-2 was pre-trained on manipulation data from $200 skill-capture gloves shipped to more than 2,000 contributors.

items.title: Agility opens a 60,000 sq ft Silicon Valley hub to train Digit
items.summary: The Digit maker's new Fremont center will focus on training, testing and advancing the AI that teaches its humanoid new skills, according to Agility — with nearly 200 AI and field-operations hires planned and more than $300 million in multi-year Digit orders behind the expansion.

items.title: LimX unveils COSA 0.5 — and Oli runs household chores with no teleop
items.summary: The freshly funded Shenzhen maker's three-layer 'agentic OS' pairs a world model and closed-loop reasoning with VLA skills — enough, according to LimX, for China's first fully autonomous long-horizon home run by a full-size humanoid.

items.title: Jim Fan: 'Robotics right now is like LLMs in 2020'
items.summary: NVIDIA's AI director told RAISE Week in Paris that humanoid prices have fallen 98% in two decades and open GR00T downloads have passed 10 million, according to Fan — with 'world action models' that predict future frames as the next paradigm.

items.title: 1X launches a World Model Lab to scale humanoid intelligence
items.summary: The NEO maker's new research organization, headed by ex-Luma researcher Samarth Sinha, will pretrain on web media, human video, simulation and robot data — world models, says CEO Bernt Børnich, will free humanoids from narrow tasks in static environments.
